newsitem.title: FRANCE: French mediator sees progress in trucker talks.
newsitem.headline: French mediator sees progress in trucker talks.

text.p: Striking French truckers and their employers made "significant progress" on several issues in negotiations on the ninth day of road blockades across the country, government mediator Robert Cros said on Tuesday.

Cros said in a statement the parties, due to resume talks at 3 p.m. (1400 GMT), had agreed in principle on changes in sick leave, travel expenses and banning trucks of all nationalities from French roads on Sundays.
"Significant progress has been accomplished, and certain issues have already been agreed in principle," Cros said. He hailed "the positive and constructive attitude of the parties".
The truckers have set up 171 blockades across the country, sealing off roads and many petrol depots to demand wage hikes, changes in working hours and retirement at 55 instead of 60.

Cros said the government had offered proposals that would enable truckers to retire early, facilitate the hiring of younger drivers and improve their safety. Another proposal, he said, would lower payroll taxes for haulage companies that cut working hours.
A fifth round of talks ended early on Tuesday morning and unions said the progress achieved was insufficient to justify easing the blockades.
